messages:
alex.cheng: heads up — saw two restore failures this morning in tenant-88. stacktrace points to KMS Decrypt failing with AccessDenied. suspect a grant was pruned by the janitor job.

maria_k: ugh. any correlation IDs or logs?

samir: can you paste the error lines?

alex.cheng: sure — from the restore worker logs:
```
2026-03-22T07:12:03Z ERROR restore_worker: decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:..
requestId=abcd-1234 tenant=tenant-88 snapshot=sn-2026-03-21-17
```

sre_jen: that looks like the grant was removed or expired. our janitor prunes stale grants older than 90d unless they have a "provenance" tag.

maria_k: do we have an audit trail showing grant deletion? cloudtrail should show GrantRevoke or RevokeGrant API calls.

alex.cheng: cloudtrail entry shows a call from service-account `kms-janitor@redwood` at 2026-03-21T06:59:01Z, reason: `cleanup: orphaned-grant`.

samir: ok so janitor triggers. why was the grant considered orphaned? we tag grants when we create them with `x-redwood-owner` + ticket id. if the tag was missing, janitor will prune.

maria_k: is there a gap in tag propagation for older snapshots? I remember a migration last year that backfilled metadata but not grant tags.

sre_jen: yep — snapshot backfill skipped tags for archives older than 1y. those grants never got the `x-redwood-provenance` tag so they look orphaned to janitor.

alex.cheng: actionables? we need restores unblocked for tenant-88 and prevent recurrence.

samir: for immediate mitigation: 1) re-issue a one-off grant to the restore principal for that key. 2) re-run the restore. 3) create a short-lived retention exception to avoid further janitor runs until we patch.

maria_k: +1. who can create the grant quickly? @sre_jen?

sre_jen: I can do it now. will create grant and tag it with `x-redwood-provenance: restore-incident/1766667777` and link ticket.

samir: while that happens, we should also patch the janitor to consult the snapshot metadata table before pruning. currently it only checks tag presence. Patch idea: janitor should query our `snapshot_ownership` index and skip prune if a snapshot references the grant.

alex.cheng: long-term we need two things: 1) longer auditlog retention for KMS Grant API events (cloudtrail), 2) permanent provenance on grants + automated reconciliation.

maria_k: on audit retention — current cloudtrail S3 retention is 90 days in staging and 365 for prod but only 60 days for some regions. we should standardize to 400 days for grant-relevant events. legal ok with 400d?

sre_jen: I'll loop in compliance, but 400d seems reasonable. also we should export KMS key rotation/grant events to our internal ELK index so SRE can query quickly.

samir: reconciliation proposal: nightly job that enumerates active snapshots and ensures every snapshot's key has an active grant with provenance metadata. If missing, create a flagged ticket and optionally auto-create a grant with justification text and TTL=30d.

maria_k: TTL auto-grant is nice, but must include who approved it. tie to ticket and require a human to close the ticket to convert TTL into permanent grant.

alex.cheng: from incident runbook perspective, add steps: 1) check cloudtrail for GrantRevoke events, 2) search `snapshot_ownership` for snapshot references, 3) if restore blocked, use `grant-quickcreate` script with parameter `--reason=restore-incident/ID`, 4) add temporary janitor hold: POST /admin/janitor/holds snapshot-key-arn.

sre_jen: example quickcreate command:
```bash
# create grant for restore role
./tools/grant-quickcreate --key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/abc123 --grantee arn:aws:iam::111:role/restore-worker --tags x-redwood-provenance=restore-incident/1766667777 --ttl 30d
```

alex.cheng: also adding an alert to our SLOs: create a synthetic job that attempts decrypting a small test blob for each tenant daily and alerts on 5xx/403. catches missing grants early.

samir: good. we should also make janitor safer: require two conditions to prune a grant: tag missing AND no snapshot referencing the key AND grant age > 180d. add an allowlist for keys used by backfills.

maria_k: compliance asks that we keep an immutable record of who created grant and justification. we can store that in the snapshot metadata (fields: grant_creator, grant_ticket, grant_created_at).

sre_jen: on it. I'll create a PR with janitor changes + quickcreate CLI + runbook updates. linking ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4123

alex.cheng: thanks. for the immediate restore I re-ran after grant creation and it succeeded. marking incident as mitigated but keeping audit open.

devops-bot: Incident SEC-4123 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Assigned: sre_jen.

maria_k: cool. follow-up items: PR review, cloudtrail retention proposal, nightly reconciliation job, runbook update. I'll consolidate into SEC-4123 checklist. :white_check_mark:
